recipes.name: Apple Enchilada Dessert
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, or more to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Spoon fruit evenly onto all tortillas and sprinkle with cinnamon. Roll up tortillas and place seam side down on a lightly greased 8x8-inch baking pan.
Bring white sugar, brown sugar, water, and margarine to a boil in a medium saucepan. Reduce heat and simmer, stirring constantly, for 3 minutes.
Pour sauce evenly over tortillas; sprinkle with extra cinnamon on top to taste.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Enchilada Dessert
raw_recipe.description: These delicious apple enchiladas are simply apples rolled in flour tortillas. They are easy and fast to make too, and can be easily customized.

review.reviewBody: Before I made this dessert I read practically every review written and therefore, made the following changes: used 2 cans of apple pie filling mixed with 1 tsp. cinnamon and 1/2 tsp nutmeg, whipped 8 oz of reduced-fat cream cheese with 1/2 cup powdered sugar and 1/4 tsp. cinnamon the mixed with the apple pie filling mixture (which I coarsely chopped with a knife and fork), reduced the water to 1/3 cup, added 1 Tbsp. cornstarch to the sauce along with 1/2 tsp. vanilla. I use five tortillas (that's how many mouths I'm feeding) and put the extra filling on top of the enchiladas. I found that even though the sauce looks thin after 3 minutes of cooking it thickens quickly as it sits. I usually put this together ahead of time in a 12x8" rectangular baking dish (and it just barely fits) and about 1 hour before time for dessert (my family likes to wait a little while after dinner) I pop it into the oven at 400 degrees for 40 minutes on the top rack. The result is a a thick sweet sauce and yummy crepe-like apple-filled dessert. Make sure to serve warm with vanilla ice cream it really complements this dessert. Anyway thanks for posting:) I've made this twice already and even with my changes it's incredibly easy to make and yummy.

A-MAZING dessert!! I made it for my inlaws and they love love loved it!!! The only difference i made was: adding a mixture of cream cheese and sugar into the middle of the tortilla before the apples. When we tried it, the cream cheese in it was soooooooo delicous! ive made it WITH and WITHOUT the cream cheese mixture, and its way better with it!! Also make sure to cook the enchiladas for a little longer than usual so that it gets a crispier crust. I highly recommend this!!!

I seen this made on a You Tube video and they said to let it sit for a full 30 min after pouring the liquid mixture over it, and that it will be soggy if you skip that step. Also don't use margarine, when margarine melts it separates and primarily is water. If you want the out come to be a tad crisp and caramel-like you have to use real butter. The butter somehow interacts w the sugars to make a caramel consistency. I added a tsp of vanilla flavor to it before I brought it to a boil. I cut the amount of water in half because I used home canned apples and they seemed thinner/wetter to me than the store bought kind. Even store brands will vary by how watery they are so you have adjust the water accordingly. These will not in any way fit in an 8x8 pan that I can see, I used a 13x9 glass pan, and made 6 using 8inch tortillas. If you cram them all up too close together they will stay soggy.

I do mine different. I buy the can of apples and dice them up very tiny then simmer on stove to cook a little. I use 8. 7 inch tortillas. Put 2 spoons in center. Fold sides leaving 2 inch opening then the other side folded over. Fry in frying pan with canola oil. Then when hot sprinkle with cinnamon sugar mix. Delicious when hot.

Very good! Made some changes after reading reviews. I used 2 cans apple pie filling and added 1 tsp cinnamon and 1/4 tsp nutmeg to it. I also, made a cream cheese mixture (beat 8oz softened cream cheese, 1/4 cup powdered sugar and 1/4 tsp cinnamon until fluffy) Spoon some cream cheese mixture onto tortillas top with apple mixture and roll. The sauce- I reduced sugars and water to 1/3 cup, added 1 Tbsp corn starch and 1/2 tsp vanilla (still very sweet- next time will try 1/4 cup each sugar) Also, put under broiler to crisp up. Only problem is the filling oozed out.

I made my own filling for these apple enchiladas, which I believe made them 5 stars! I used 3 large Granny Smith apples, 1/2 c. sugar, 1 T. flour, 1 t. cinnamon, and a shake of nutmeg. The apples will supply the moisture while they are baking. You can also make the sauce ahead of time. I reduced the 1/2 cup water in the sauce to 1/3 cup this helped avoid having the runny sauce that so many reviewers complained of, and cooked it until thickened...not just 3 minutes. I baked them for 40 minutes. These were great!

I was craving some sort of apple desset tonight and stumbled upon this little gem. It is incredible! I used 2 fresh Eastern apples, mixed with 1/8 cup sugar and 1 tbsp flour and the tsp of cinnamon. I cut the sugars for the sauce in half and probably could have cut even more. I baked it for 30 minutes at 350. absolutely, insanely delicious. Thank you for the recipe!

PS - I made just the sauce and poured it over some fresh peaches and vanilla ice cream. SO INCREDIBLY DELICIOUS!

This is a wonderful desert!!! Love the crispy tortilla. Read through many reviews so I cut the sugars and water to 1/3 cup each and sprinkled the apple pie filling with the recommended cinnamon and also added apple pie spice. And finally I used 1 tsp cornstarch to thicken the sauce and added 1 tsp vanilla. Thank you so much for submitting this! I know I made additions but I would never have made these in the first place if I hadn't found this. Going to a house warming party and plan on making a tray of them. Yum!

You can't hardly go wrong with butter, sugar, and cinnamon mixed!! I am not a fan at all of cooked apples but, this is at the top of my dessert list. The only change I made was using fresh apples. I peeled and cut four delicious red apples and mixed them with the cinnamon before putting them in the tortillas (this ended up doubling the recipe, so I made two pans and shared one). They are best this way if the fresh apples are refrigerated for a few days mixed with the cinnamon, that's how I did my second pan and it was better than the first. The third time I cooked it I went by the recipe and used canned apples and it was good but, I'm just not a fan of canned apples so I'll continue to use fresh apples.

This was surprisingly delicious! Very easy, and quick.I used the tortilla land uncooked flour tortillas(costco sells them) for fresh tortillas. I made my own peach pie filling from scratch. I placed 1/4 cup of that in the middle of the warm tortillas I just made. Followed the rest of the recipe, and it was the bomb! Some rich vanilla ice cream complimented this great recipe.

I used 8 small apples sauteed with 2 tbsps brown sugar, 1/4 tsp cinnamon and 1/4 c apple juice for the pie filling. This filled 8 seven inch whole wheat tortillas. For the syrup I used 1 tbsp butter, 1/4 c each brown and white sugar, 1/4 c water, 1/4 tsp cinnamon and a splash of vanilla. We really enjoyed this with vanilla ice cream.
Used 12” tortillas in a 9x13 baking pan. 4 of them fit perfectly. Used 1/2 cup butter and 3/4 cup brown sugar. Topped with sugar/cinnamon mix. Really yummy!!👍
Baked cinnamon apples were always one of my favorite treats. A surprisingly nice touch using the tortilla. Will make again!

So yummy! I did a bigger batch so it filled a 9x13 dish, but ended up only using half the sauce and it turned out perfectly after baking 25 minutes. I also did half a cup less sugar, and next time I'm going to try butter instead of margarine. An easy, affordable and instant classic!

My sons loved this!! They asked me to make them a fun breakfast today and I had some apples that needed to be used. I made my own homemade apple pie filling to sub in for the canned stuff. Definitely delicious!
Made it exactly they were not crispy, the were really really soggy.

While I had purchased a 21oz can of strawberry pie filling, my S.I.L. had brought a huge batch of freshly picked strawberries to family vacay and I decided to give this recipe a try. Delicious and a huge hit with kids and adults alike! Lesson learned; fresh berries have water content that if I had thought of it, I would have added a TBLS or 2 of flour in so when baked, the filling would be thicker - like pie filling. But, the crowd raved, each topped with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. A fun dessert! Thanks ReDonna!! I will make again!

When I made the filled tortillas (6) and put them in an 8x8 baking dish, after pouring the sauce over them, they were sitting in a pool of sauce. Is this how they're supposed to be or is 8x8 the wrong sized baking dish. Not sure if they'll be soggy, I just put them in the oven. Thanks for any help.
